series.title: Real GDP growth
series.sub: Annualized change from the prior quarter
series.note: Chained 2017 dollars. Each quarter is revised twice after the advance estimate; the third estimate arrives about three months after the quarter ends.

series.title: Nominal GDP
series.sub: Current dollars, seasonally adjusted annual rate
series.note: The level series is the denominator for the debt and deficit ratios below. Use the log scale to read growth rates off the slope.

series.title: Labor productivity growth
series.sub: Nonfarm business output per hour, change from a year earlier
series.note: Computed here as the four-quarter change in the output-per-hour index.

meta.title: Nonfarm Business Sector: Labor Productivity (Output per Hour) for All Workers

series.title: Unemployment rate
series.sub: Civilian labor force, ages 16 and over
series.note: From the household survey. The broader U-6 measure, which adds discouraged and involuntary part-time workers, can be added as a companion tile.

series.title: Labor force participation
series.sub: Share of the population aged 16 and over in the labor force
series.note: The long decline since 2000 is mostly aging; the prime-age rate next door strips that out.

series.title: Prime-age employment rate
series.sub: Employed share of the population aged 25 to 54

series.title: Payroll employment, monthly change
series.note: First-differenced from the payroll level. The two most recent months are preliminary and get revised with each release. April 2020 dwarfs everything else; a range button trims it.

series.title: Consumer price inflation
series.sub: CPI, all items, change from a year earlier
series.note: Twelve-month change in the index. Core CPI and the median CPI are easy companions.

meta.title: Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers: All Items in U.S. City Average

series.title: Core PCE inflation
series.sub: Personal consumption expenditures excluding food and energy, change from a year earlier
series.note: The Federal Reserve's preferred gauge against its 2 percent objective.

meta.title: Personal Consumption Expenditures Excluding Food and Energy (Chain-Type Price Index)

series.title: Federal funds rate
series.next: Posted every business day; the monthly average settles after month end

series.title: 10-year Treasury yield
series.note: The daily series is available too; a 10-year minus 2-year spread tile is a natural addition.

meta.title: Market Yield on U.S. Treasury Securities at 10-Year Constant Maturity, Quoted on an Investment Basis

series.next: Posted every business day; the monthly average settles after month end

series.title: Debt held by the public
series.note: Excludes debt held in government accounts such as the Social Security trust funds. Gross debt is the tile next door.

meta.title: Federal Debt Held by the Public as Percent of Gross Domestic Product

series.title: Federal budget balance
series.sub: Surplus or deficit as a share of GDP, by fiscal year
series.note: The monthly Treasury statements give a running fiscal-year-to-date figure between annual updates.

meta.title: Federal Surplus or Deficit [-] as Percent of Gross Domestic Product

series.title: Total public debt
series.sub: Debt to the penny, latest business day
series.freq_label: Daily since April 1993, shown at month ends; quarterly before that

series.title: Real median family income
series.note: Published once a year in September from the Current Population Survey, covering the previous calendar year. The weekly earnings tile moves quarterly in between.

meta.title: Real Median Family Income in the United States
meta.release_name: Income and Poverty in the United States

series.release_name: Income and Poverty in the United States

series.title: Real median weekly earnings
series.sub: Full-time wage and salary workers, 1982 to 1984 dollars
series.note: The 2020 jump is composition; low-wage workers left employment faster than others.

meta.title: Employed full time: Median usual weekly real earnings: Wage and salary workers: 16 years and over
meta.release_name: Weekly and Hourly Earnings from the Current Population Survey

series.release_name: Weekly and Hourly Earnings from the Current Population Survey

series.title: Net international migration
series.sub: Census population estimates, year ending June 30
series.note: Revised substantially with each vintage. The 2010s come from the intercensal series and the 2020s from the latest vintage; 2020 sums the two partial periods.

series.title: Foreign-born share of the labor force
series.sub: Current Population Survey, not seasonally adjusted
series.note: Foreign-born labor force divided by foreign-born plus native-born labor force. Monthly CPS immigration data are noisy; a 12-month average is an option.

meta.title: Civilian Labor Force Level - Foreign Born

series.title: Foreign-born labor force
series.sub: Civilian labor force, ages 16 and over
series.note: Compare with the year-ago value rather than the prior month; the series is not seasonally adjusted.

meta.title: Civilian Labor Force Level - Foreign Born

comp.title: Federal spending by category
comp.freq_label: Monthly, accumulated over the fiscal year (October to September)
comp.note: The snapshot is the current fiscal year to date and compares with the same months a year earlier; once the September statement posts in mid-October it covers the full year. The history uses complete fiscal years, which on FiscalData begin with 2016. Medicare is shown gross of premiums; Medicaid sits inside Health.

comp.title: Federal revenue by source
comp.freq_label: Monthly, accumulated over the fiscal year (October to September)
comp.note: The snapshot is the current fiscal year to date and compares with the same months a year earlier. Payroll taxes combine employment and general retirement, unemployment insurance, and other retirement receipts.
